items.title: 68356_Howard R. Scott oral history interview
items.q: The mention of Harry Truman is made by the interviewer in a prose summary, not by the interviewee, and the interviewee does not respond to or reference this specific mention in the provided text.

ctx.x: That was -- we were talking about Benny Carter. It was around that time. Something had happened, and I couldn't remember what it was, but this is what happened. This came after that, after I started with Benny. It came after that, yeah.

Then after the war was over, Harry Truman was President. That was cool, because the other guys came back. Well, then, that was the height of what you'd call the Depression or whatever it was, there weren't any big bands, the shows were closing, the big shows, the Capitol, the Strand, Broadway. Of course, the Paramount, that was still going.
And up in Harlem, everyplace was closing (inaudible), everyplace was closing. So there wasn't much work to be done. But there was a fellow that was getting jobs. You ever hear of Fess Finley?
